Every run writes a replay journal, and `bernstein replay latest --verify` recomputes the journal head. Each coding task gets its own git worktree behind merge gates. candidates.demonstrated_gap: The overturn condition names approval waits and effect recovery beyond native workers, and Paperclip's control plane documents both. Its CLI docs cover a headless path: `ao start` runs the daemon in the background, alongside `ao spawn` and `ao session kill/restore/resume-agent`. It is kept for comparison rather than trial for three reasons: the README install path is desktop downloads, and the standalone `ao` binary is built from a source checkout; telemetry sends the signed-in GitHub username on session start unless telemetry is turned off; and its review loop depends on a forge PR flow. candidates.demonstrated_gap:
The winners supply no VM boundary, no resource caps and no hostile-workload qualification (open gap 5). srt's network evidence covers only temporary IPv4 loopback HTTP (open gap 1). BoxLite v0.10.4 runs each box as a hardware-virtualized VM (KVM / Hypervisor.framework) inside an OS sandbox (seccomp / sandbox-exec), with CPU/memory/resource limits, an allow_net egress allowlist and host-side secret injection (README Features). Its narrower discriminators over the other no-credential local VM candidates are twofold. First, among those candidates only its README lists a Windows (WSL2) x86_64 row ('WSL2 with KVM support, user in kvm group'); microsandbox and Brig document Linux and macOS but no WSL2 row. Second, it documents a seccomp/sandbox-exec layer around the VM. All four published advisories are fixed at v0.10.4:
- Two critical advisories were patched in 0.9.0.
- High GHSA-c7v3 (allow_net Host/SNI versus dialed-IP bypass) and medium GHSA-xjhv (exec timeout bypass) are both listed without a patched version. A code read at the tag (not executed) shows both fixed. Hostname-authorized egress now dials the name through host-side resolution and discards the guest's destination IP (fix commits #1330 2026-08-25 and #1495 2026-09-18). Exec timeouts escalate from SIGTERM to SIGKILL.

Four advisories in 2026, including the same allowlist-bypass class as microsandbox's GHSA-3mpp, are a maintenance fact the trial must probe. Trial precondition, an operator host change and not a refutation: this host's /dev/kvm is crw-rw---- root:systemd-resolve and the user is not in that group, so the documented kvm-group step alone will not grant access.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn:
A bounded native trial of BoxLite v0.10.4 against srt 0.0.77, first on linux-wsl2 and then on macOS arm64, reusing the srt receipt fixtures:
1. Filesystem permit/deny, including the overlapping denied read/write path (open gap 4).
2. Network egress with TLS, DNS, IPv6 and a remote host.
3. A Host/SNI-allowlisted name sent to a non-matching IP.
4. An allowlisted name that resolves to loopback, 169.254.169.254 or private address space, including a DNS-rebinding case. This is an untested boundary: at v0.10.4 the link-local check reads the guest-chosen address, and whether the host-side resolution in egress_dialer.go filters such results was not read.
5. A memory hog and a CPU hog that must be capped, and an exec timeout that must kill a process that ignores SIGTERM.
6. No residual processes, mounts, QCOW2 disks or state directories after removal.

BoxLite is adopted for untrusted workloads only if, on both hosts, it enforces every axis srt enforces plus resource caps, with clean teardown. Any reproduced allowlist bypass, uncapped hog or leftover state refutes it.

Claude Code installs through a plugin marketplace and Codex through `engram setup codex`. v2.2.0 and v2.2.1 (2026-09-25) bind Codex MCP writes to the runtime session identity and honor CODEX_HOME. Git Sync exports compressed chunks to another machine, which offers a path to the independent-host recovery that the winner has not qualified. candidates.demonstrated_gap: The current path keeps no re-verifiable record of a cited page. ctx_fetch_and_index stores converted markdown with a 24 h default TTL and removes stored content older than 14 days (installed tool description). agent-browser 0.38.1 can save a HAR, a PDF and rendered text (README@v0.38.1 L145, L194-195, L371-374), but none of them records the TLS certificate chain or a provenance statement, and no layer receipt in the input shows them used as citation evidence. Scoop is a single-page 'witnessing the web' capture engine. It writes WARC, warc.gz or WACZ with a provenance summary and SSL-certificate attachments on by default, plus an optional PDF snapshot. It writes a JSON capture summary even for failed captures, uses an isolated browsing context per capture, and signs WACZ through an authsign-compatible endpoint. A trial is feasible now on the Linux workstation: Node v24.21.0 is present, npm engines require node>=22.0.0, and the README lists Linux, Mac OS and WSL. Caveats: (a) the README documents no page-text index, so quotes must be re-verified from the WARC payload or the PDF text; (b) the default provenance step calls icanhazip.com; (c) postinstall.sh downloads yt-dlp 2026.08.19 and crip 2.1.0 with pinned SHA-256, and on every Mac it fetches crip-macos-amd64 (Rosetta on M5 is unverified); (d) signing needs an authsign server, which is out of scope for a first trial.

For static pages it adds wget --warc-file (wget 1.21.4 on Linux; unverified on the Macs). It is overturned if C0 matches (1) and (2) and the frozen citation checks do not require the extra provenance.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: One open gap is still open: Promptfoo and Inspect AI have not been compared on the same frozen cases. The 2026-09-26 sweep proposed a 60-case comparison, but no run is retained. Inspect 0.3.264-0.3.272 (16-28 Sep 2026) has since added failure-preserving behavior that bears directly on this layer's negative-control and fresh-case requirements. (a) Empty or whitespace completions are now scored with reason="no_response", so a model that returned nothing is distinguishable from one that answered wrong (0.3.269). (b) Samples cut off by a cancellation that Inspect did not issue are recorded as sample errors instead of scored as completed (0.3.269). (c) eval_set tops up a dataset that has grown with stable sample ids by running only the new samples (0.3.270). That fits adding freshly labeled cases without rerunning or re-tuning on the old ones. (d) human_reviewer() lets an operator review a tool call together with its result (0.3.264). (e) `inspect score --scorer pkg/name` resolves @scanner functions from installed packages (0.3.266). Promptfoo's retained evidence (4 upstream pairs and a 2-assertion echo fixture) exercises none of these conditions. This establishes trial value, not superiority.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Extend the recorded 60-case plan. Run Promptfoo 0.123.1 and Inspect 0.3.272 on the same frozen, independently labeled semantic-advice/extraction cases: identical recorded outputs, identical mock tool responses and the same judge model. Inject wrong-ticker, look-ahead-date, missing-tool and grader-error mutations. Add two negative-control arms: empty output, and an externally cancelled sample. Inspect joins or replaces Promptfoo only if it (1) catches more injected mutations, or labels both control arms distinctly (no_response or sample error) where Promptfoo scores them as ordinary pass or fail, and (2) keeps per-sample logs that locate each failure. Then add 20 newly labeled cases and confirm that eval_set runs only those. If the two tools reach parity on detection and failure localization, Promptfoo stays and Inspect stays keep_but_compare.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: Install-time known-malware blocking for host and agent-run installs. No running control covers this axis. The incumbents act in CI on committed files only: osv-scanner v2.6.0 (security-scan.yml) matches committed lockfiles against OSV, which carries OpenSSF MAL- records; dependency-review-action v5.0.0 gates PR diffs; harden-runner v2.21.1 audits egress without blocking. Host installs have no lockfile to scan: npm -g installs without a shrinkwrap, uv tool installs whose transitive PyPI dependencies are unlocked, the upstream launcher 'npx -y --prefer-online socraticode@latest' (docs/token-efficiency-stack.json:2978) and 'uvx --from git+...serena@c6fbd1c' (docs/foundation-stack.md:115). safe-chain wraps npm, npx, yarn, pnpm, pnpx, bun, bunx, pip, pip3, uv, uvx, poetry, pipx and pdm through a local proxy. It needs no token or account. Its README states that no build data is shared; this is a vendor claim, and its egress has not been observed. The malware database is bulk JSON (malware_predictions.json and malware_pypi.json from malware-list.aikido.dev), and a mirror can serve it (malwareListBaseUrl). A trial can therefore pin it by snapshot hash, which the layer's overturn_when requires. The 1.5.21 linux-x64 binary carries a GitHub in-toto attestation, so its provenance can be verified, unlike the checksum-only Syft install. Its 48-hour age gate adds nothing over a configured 7-day native cooldown: npm min-release-age exists since npm 11.10.0, and a user-level uv.toml exclude-newer duration governs uv tool and uvx. The 48-hour gate is also shorter than windows such as tj-actions (about 3 days) and Kong (about 10 days) in Woodruff's sample. The increment to test is therefore the denylist alone. It matters for installs made after a feed flags a version whose attack window outlasts the cooldown, and for installs that bypass the cooldown. TLS interception with an injected CA bundle (registryProxy/certBundle.js, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS) is inferred from source paths only; the code was not read.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Isolate the denylist from the age gate. (1) Offline and read-only first: hash a snapshot of Aikido's malware_predictions.json and malware_pypi.json, then diff it against the OSV MAL- records (ossf/malicious-packages) for npm and PyPI incidents of the last 90 days, comparing presence and first-seen time. If Aikido's entries are a subset of OSV MAL with no lead time, the incumbent replicates the blocker: resolve a lock or SBOM, run osv-scanner v2.6.0, then install. That result overturns this proposal. (2) Bounded host trial on linux-wsl2, then macos-arm64, in a scratch HOME with the --ci PATH shims and no rc-file edits. Verify the binary with 'gh attestation verify'. Set the age gate to 0 against native npm min-release-age=7 and a user-level uv.toml exclude-newer = '7 days'. Replay the stack's real install set in non-interactive shells: the bootstrap pins, uv tool installs, and the npx socraticode and uvx serena launches. Any of the following overturns it: a false block, a broken sha256-pinned or --ignore-scripts install, a CA bundle that leaks beyond the wrapped subprocess, or egress other than the registries and malware-list.aikido.dev. The vendor test packages safe-chain-test and safe-chain-pi-test prove the plumbing only, not detection quality. (3) Scope: host and ad-hoc installs only. Committed lockfiles stay with osv-scanner, so no dependency has two owners.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: The gap is runtime enforcement of action pins, not transitive coverage. All 13 distinct actions in the 20 workflows are SHA-pinned, and the repository's Actions policy reports sha_pinning_required: true. zizmor's online impostor-commit audit checks, statically at PR time, whether a pinned commit belongs to the repository itself or only to its fork network. Nothing enforces at run time that a locked commit sits on a branch of the named repository or that the repository identity has not been redirected. gh-actions-lock is GitHub's technical-preview extension for Workflow Dependency Pinning. It writes .github/workflows/actions.lock and, for onboarded workflows, blocks at run time any unlocked dependency, forged lock entry, commit not reachable from a branch, or repository redirect. It gives no transitive benefit here today: 12 of the 13 actions are node24 actions with no nested uses, none is composite, and there are no local actions. The one docker action, ossf/scorecard-action, runs docker://ghcr.io/ossf/scorecard-action:v2.4.4 by tag, and lock coverage of that image is unverified. Two things block it. Dependabot's weekly github-actions PRs are expected to change workflow SHAs without updating actions.lock until the announced Dependabot integration ships (not observed), which would split ownership of the same pins. The public-preview roadmap item github/roadmap#1253 is still open, so enforcement on Free public repositories is unconfirmed.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: On a throwaway branch, onboard all 20 workflows with gh-actions-lock pinned to v0.1.6 (or the release current at trial time) and run them hosted. (2) A lock entry with a mutated SHA, an impostor fork-network commit and a renamed-repository redirect each stop the run before any job starts. (3) A Dependabot github-actions PR on the onboarded branch either updates actions.lock or fails visibly. Stay deferred while any of these fails. The baseline is zizmor 1.30.1's online impostor-commit audit plus the sha_pinning_required policy on the same commit.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: The winner's own open recovery case, which configuration can now test. Under the 2026-09-23 preregistered SIGKILL protocol (150 s bound, no scheduler), Dagu 2.16.6 failed: retries were refused for the whole bound. A post-hoc scheduler variant recovered in 181.4 s and 182.6 s. Temporal passed at 15 s, but with a tuned 5 s heartbeat timeout, and the record states the recovery setups 'were not equivalent'. Dagu's configuration reference makes stale-run detection tunable, with defaults proc.stale_threshold 90s, scheduler.zombie_detection_interval 45s and scheduler.failure_threshold 3 ('Consecutive stale checks before marking a run as failed'). Those defaults are arithmetically consistent with the ~182 s (90 s plus two or three 45 s checks), but the cause is not proven. Proc liveness 'appl[ies] to all locally owned DAG runs', yet zombie detection is a scheduler setting, so the no-scheduler protocol left the killed run in running state (inference from the reference plus the failed run). The pin is also behind. v2.17.2 (2026-09-25) is latest. 2.17.0's recovery-relevant fixes (#2775 'stop dropping queued retries', #2809 'wait for durable status before continuing past a node') have only a graceful stop/retry parity receipt, and SIGKILL was not re-run. 2.17.2 adds #2838 (resume independent branches while tasks wait), #2847 (replace stdout/stderr artifact per attempt) and dagu start --only (#2855). candidates.demonstrated_gap: Among self-contained server binaries, Restate is the only surveyed engine that addresses loss of the server host itself, not just a worker (open gap 1). Its cluster docs say that running at least 2*default-replication-1 nodes tolerates default-replication-1 node failures, and 2n+1 metadata-server nodes tolerate n metadata failures. So the WSL2 workstation plus both Macs (3 nodes, replication 2) could lose any one host. None of the other candidates does this without replicating an external database: Temporal's dev server keeps state in one SQLite file, Dagu relies on one coordinator, DBOS and Absurd rely on one Postgres, and Conductor and Kestra (HA is Enterprise-only) reach it only through replicated external backends. v1.7.12 (2026-09-22) ships restate-server for aarch64-apple-darwin and x86_64-unknown-linux-musl. The 2026-09-26 sweep refuted it only through the GPT-6 fit vote's license veto ('a policy exclusion'), while the Claude fit vote kept it. With licenses now information only, that refutation does not stand on merit. It is compare, not trial, for four reasons. It was never executed on the frozen cases ('Dagster and Restate were not executed'). No real job has shown it needs to survive server-host loss (paper runs are one-shot systemd-run units with Restart=no). The docs carry operating cost: replacing a node needs a snapshot repository (object store or manual filesystem export), and 'If you have lost all nodes which previously hosted this partition, you have permanent data loss'. And there is an unverified WSL2 risk: the Macs must reach the workstation node inbound, which needs mirrored networking or a port proxy. Process-tree cancellation would also need handler adapter code, as with Temporal.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Port compare.py's four frozen cases to a Restate Python service adapter. Carry the fixture checkpoint as a journaled step result or keep the work directory on a shared mount. Form a 3-node cluster (WSL2 plus both Macs, replication 2, snapshot repository configured) and kill the node leading the finalize invocation's partition mid-finalize.
Restate passes if a surviving node completes within 150 s with checkpoint reuse, no duplicate completed.json and zero descendants on every host, and a cancel bounds the subprocess tree. Record node processes, setup steps and snapshot-store burden against Temporal's single-server arm.
A pass plus a real job that must survive server-host loss makes Restate the targeted challenger. It becomes not_adopted if the cluster cannot form across WSL2 and macOS or fails the kill case.

WSL x86_64 to Mac arm64 restore is therefore logical only: pg_dump/pg_restore carried by the retained Restic. Over the in-winner physical path (pg_basebackup --incremental, pg_combinebackup, pg_verifybackup, a hand-written archive_command), pgBackRest adds a maintained same-architecture PITR pipeline. PG 25.3 says pg_dump 'cannot be used as part of a continuous-archiving solution' and that archive commands 'should generally be designed to refuse to overwrite any pre-existing archive file'. pgBackRest's WAL push de-duplicates identical segments and 'otherwise an error is raised'. A WinGet Configuration file is declarative YAML applied through WinGet and PowerShell DSC resources. `winget configure test -f <file>` checks the system against the desired state. `validate` and `export --package-id` exist. The WinGetPackage DSC resource has Id, Source, Version and UseLatest properties, so a WSL version pin can be declared. A Brewfile `winget` entry documents only id: and source:, so brew bundle cannot carry that pin. general: Method and skills. Skills used: search-first and iterative-retrieval (this schema has no skills_used field). Each candidate class was checked against catalogs/, docs/, blueprints/, evidence/, adoption/ and manifests/ at origin/main b2767df2, and against the proposed and refuted lists of the ledger's 09-23 and 09-26 sweeps. Every repository named above was then checked with gh api repos/<r>/commits?since=2026-07-01. All had a default-branch commit inside the 90-day window, and none is archived. Three WebSearch calls (MCP spec, embedding models, OCR models) served only as leads; facts come from repository records and the GitHub and HF APIs. Token lanes: ctx_execute for repo-wide git grep and JSON derivation with scratch-file reads, and shell gh api for maintenance facts.

Systematic bias: candidates must be GitHub repositories, so model releases published only on Hugging Face cannot be proposed. None of the 155 proposals on 09-29 is an HF model card. Model axes live only in separately frozen plans: local-inference-latest-20260926 varies the model on llama.cpp alone, and the 09-26 semantic-rag return judged Nemotron-3-Embed-1B on vLLM. The document-retrieval return itself names OvisOCR2 as 'HF only'. Add an HF model-card lane that takes maintenance dates from the HF API.

Structural gap: the foundation has no local-inference layer. manifests/candidates.json keeps TensorRT-LLM at 'watch' and files it under semantic-rag for that reason, while the 09-26 seeds placed it under observation-inference (evidence/artifacts/landscape-sweep-20260926/README.md). Engine candidates therefore fall between observation-inference and semantic-rag, and the hybrid CPU+GPU MoE engines were judged only in the trading layer agents-models-workers.

Yield and fit-lens calibration: five layers ended with zero survivors after both refuters (native-clients, observation-inference, hosting-services, recovery-portability, mcp-surfaces). The Claude fit lens refuted 97 of 155 proposals and the GPT-6 fit lens 61. The lenses disagree most in workers (7 vs 1), instructions-skills (7 vs 2), git-github-automation (7 vs 2) and mcp-surfaces (7 vs 3). The disagreement runs the other way in quality-evaluation (2 vs 5) and scheduling-supervision (0 vs 3). Calibrate both lenses on a known-good control per layer. For zero-survivor layers, widen the candidate classes instead of re-running the same pool.

Incumbency rather than evidence, per each layer's own open gaps: durable-memory's ai-memory is a retained control ('No matched semantic-recall or usefulness benchmark between ai-memory and any alternative exists'). The token-efficiency winners have 'No matched baseline ... for the current native tasks'. code-navigation's serena has 'No matched cross-candidate benchmark'. quality-evaluation's promptfoo rests on 'one upstream example with 4 pairs plus a 2-assertion echo fixture'. For instructions-skills, 'No winner has a measured improvement in task quality or provider cost'. For workers, 'No executed head-to-head comparison exists'. web-research's tavily-cli needs a Tavily credential, and the layer records no measured comparison with the native client web tools; its only comparison gap is agent-browser vs Playwright CLI.
